newsitem.title: USA: CellPro to appeal $2.3 mln jury award.
newsitem.headline: CellPro to appeal $2.3 mln jury award.

text.p: CellPro Inc said on Tuesday it would appeal against a $2.3 million jury award in a patent lawsuit over the use of an antibody for use in bone marrow transplants.

The jury award in Federal District Court of Delaware to Baxter International Inc, Becton Dickinson & Co and Johns Hopkins University could rise, since the jury has determined that CellPro willfully infringed upon the patents, CellPro said.
Damages were based on royalties on past sales of the CellPro products which included this antibody.

In a trial concluded in August 1995, involving the same parties in the same court, a jury found both the two patents in dispute, as well as two additional patents asserted against CellPro, to be invalid and not infringed by CellPro, it said.
The court, in response to plaintiffs' post-trial motions, declined to enter the jury verdict and instead ordered a new trial, CellPro said.

Since the initial jury verdict, the CEPRATE SC System received FDA approval in December 1996 for use in bone marrow transplants and more than 5,000 patients worldwide have been treated using the system, CellPro said.
